title: RAGO: Systematic Performance Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Serving
technique: RAGSchema abstraction plus exhaustive analytical search over task placement, resource allocation and batching policies for RAG pipelines, producing a TTFT vs QPS/chip Pareto frontier

optimized_metrics.evidence: schedules to identify Pareto frontier for key performance metrics ... such as TTFT and QPS/Chip.
RAGO performs an exhaustive search across potentially millions of schedules to identify Pareto frontier for key performance metrics such as TTFT and QPS/Chip.
[QPS/Chip] Queries-Per-Second/Chip ↦ QPS normalized by chip count, reflecting system cost efficiency.
these two phases affect different performance metrics with different SLAs: time-to-first-token (TTFT) for the prefix phase and time-per-output-token (TPOT) for the decode phase.
optimized_metrics.locator: §2 (txt line 328-330); TPOT studied via batching policies in §5/§8

headline_claim.text: RAGO achieves up to a 2× increase in QPS per chip and a 55% reduction in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: [TTFT] Time-to-First-Token ↦ average latency from request reception to the generation of the first output token.
metric_definitions.notes: In RAG, TTFT covers the whole pre-generation pipeline (query rewrite, retrieval, rerank, prefix), not only LLM prefill; computed analytically/by simulator. Prefix stage is deterministic so exact TTFT is reported.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: [TPOT] Time-Per-Output-Token ↦ average latency between generating each output token in a sequence.
metric_definitions.notes: Because of continuous batching they report the worst-case TPOT: 'we report the worst-case TPOT latency' since sequences are at different generation stages.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: [QPS] Queries-Per-Second ↦ maximum throughput, or the number of requests the system can process per second.
metric_definitions.notes: Footnote: 'queries' here is end-to-end RAG requests, not retrieval queries. End-to-end QPS is set by the slowest pipeline stage (the paper's formula is written QPS_RAG = max(QPS_i), apparently a typo for min).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: [QPS/Chip] Queries-Per-Second/Chip ↦ QPS normalized by chip count, reflecting system cost efficiency.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-XPU-chip throughput as cost-efficiency proxy; chips = ML accelerators (CPU servers for retrieval not counted in chip denominator).

slo_spec: No fixed SLO; Pareto frontier over TTFT vs QPS/Chip; user-defined performance objectives select the schedule; TTFT/TPOT SLAs mentioned generically.
load_regime: analytical/simulated max-throughput with batch-size sweeps (retrieval, prefix, decode batch); not a request-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Larger batch sizes improve retrieval and prefix throughput but may stall decoding (TPOT up); throughput vs TTFT Pareto trade-off; iterative-retrieval batching causes decode idleness (up to 2.77x normalized decode latency).
hardware: modeled XPU (generic systolic-array accelerator, TPU v5e-like) plus CPU retrieval servers (ScaNN model)
models: Llama-style 1B/8B/70B/405B generative LLMs; encoder, rewriter, reranker models in RAGSchema
workloads: four RAG paradigms: hyperscale retrieval, long-context via RAG, iterative retrieval, query rewriter + reranker
extractor_notes: Optimizer outputs a Pareto frontier rather than a single scalar; TTFT and QPS/chip are the two frontier axes. TPOT is reported (worst case) and drives batching analysis but is not a frontier axis in main results. Request-level RAG pipeline latency, not multi-call agent PROGRAM_JCT.
